newsitem.title: CHINA: Cathay Pac cargo turnover up in 1st half.
newsitem.headline: Cathay Pac cargo turnover up in 1st half.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Wednesday its cargo business reported a turnover growth of 13.6 percent in the first six month of 1997.
Turnover totalled HK$2.98 billion or US$383 million, representing about 20.5 percent of Cathay Pacific's total traffic turnover, it said in a statement.
Cathay Pacific carried 299.82 million tonnes of cargo in the six month period, up 13.80 percent and cargo revenue tonne km rose 18.40 percent against a 5.3 percent rise in cargo capacity.
The Hong Kong flag carrier posted a 1997 interim net profit of HK$1.07 billion, down 35 percent from a year earlier.
But James Barrington, Cathay Pacific's general manager for cargo, said it had been a very good first half for the cargo side of the operation.
"We have exceeded out targets and taken advantage of some excellent opportunities to boost yields and revenue," he said in the statement.
Kai Tak airport was very full and they were gearing up for a large growth spurt when the Chek Lap Kok airport opens, he added.
Hong Kong's new airport at Chek Lap Kok is scheduled to open in April 1998. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
